new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked: (and its extraction). The quoted passage is at lines 400-403 of exactly as reported ("Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length) / Stress is predictable. Stress is on the syllable with é or on the closed syllable. / é : a.ri.'é 'together' ka.'ké 'fish' / the closed syllable :'dum.ba 'bush' i.'qis, 'mosquito' tu.'qan 'night'"); I re-extracted word/document.xml from the docx independently and the same four lines come out character-for-character (curly apostrophes as stress marks included), so is faithful. Surrounding context read: the section sits between the diphthong examples and 'Syllable Patterns' (V, VV, VC, VVC, CV, CVC, CVV, CVVC with examples), followed by 'C…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive and predictable: it falls on a syllable containing the open-mid vowel é /ɛ/, otherwise on a closed (CVC) syllable, wherever that syllable sits in the word (final in a.ri.'é, ka.'ké, i.'qis, tu.'qan; initial in 'dum.ba). The sheet gives no default for words with neither, nor a tie-break for words with several heavy syllables.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; no statement for all-light words or for competition between an é-syllable and a closed syllable.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress on isolated citation forms in an SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet; tone and length not claimed (long consonants analysed as geminate clusters across a syllable boundary).
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD covers the Wagi language as a whole (villages Kamba, Silibob, Kauris, Mis, Foran); examples appear to be in the Kamba-Kauris-Silibob variety with one form flagged 'Mis dialect'. Glottolog wagi1249 has no dialect-level codes. The 'Aeschliman 1988' source named by the earlier scan is a Nobonob [gaw] item cited on Glottolog only for subclassification, not a Wagi description.

sources.note: Section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)': 'Stress is predictable. Stress is on the syllable with é or on the closed syllable.' Examples a.ri.'é 'together', ka.'ké 'fish'; 'dum.ba 'bush', i.'qis 'mosquito', tu.'qan 'night'. Nothing on secondary stress or on words lacking both é and a closed syllable.
